newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian manufacturers see stable prices in Q1.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian manufacturers see stable prices in Q1.

text.p: A majority of Malaysian manufacturers polled in a survey expect the prices of manufactured items to remain stable in the first quarter of 1997, the national Bernama news agency said on Thursday.

In a survey conducted by the Malaysian Institute of Economic Research (MIER), 59 percent of the firms polled, said they expected no change in the prices of food, textiles, wood, paper, rubber, plastics, metal and electrical products in the present quarter, Bernama reported.
The news agency was quoting a report by MIER called the Business Conditions Survey, which is designed to track economic activity in the manufacturing sector.

However, the trend indicated that there was an increase in the number of firms that expected prices to drop, compared to a fall in the number of firms that expected prices to remain stable, said Bernama.
"On a quarterly basis, the percentage of firms that expected prices to remain stable declined by 15 percentage points and those expecting a drop increased by 12 percentage points," said the report.
The report added: "The most prominent feature in the first quarter of 1997 will be a likely increase in manufacturing wages across the board."

Of the firms surveyed, 64 percent expected wage costs to increase in the first quarter, MIER said, adding that the wage increases would be highest in the wood, paper, chemical, rubber, metal, electrical and machinery sectors.
However, 73 percent of the companies surveyed anticipated no change in employment conditions in the first quarter of 1997 compared with 60 prcent in the corresponding period last year.
Meanwhile, 23 percent of them expected employment to rise in the first quarter this year compared to 32 percent in the same period last year.
"Only 40 percent of the firms surveyed expected a rise in production volume in the next three months compared with 51 percent in the third quarter of 1996," said MIER.
It said the growth prospects for the manufacturing sector in the present quarter would hinge more on increases in exports than domestic sales.

"Thirty-six percent of all firms surveyed reported an expected increase in external sales which represented no change on a yearly basis but a rise of two percentage points over the third quarter's expectation," said MIER.
Thirty-four percent of the companies surveyed expected domestic sales to increase in the first quarter, compared to 47 percent recorded in the same period last year.
